title: ALMA view of the <SUP>12</SUP>C/<SUP>13</SUP>C isotopic ratio in starburst galaxies
question: What are the 12C/13C isotope ratios and their spatial variations in the nuclear regions of NGC 253, NGC 1068 and NGC 4945, measured from 12CN and 13CN N=1-0?

evidence.quote: $^{12}$CN $N$ = 1–0 data of NGC 253 are therefore taken from (cite: Meier2015) in this work.

what.value: Single-dish 12CN/13CN integrated intensities and 12C/13C ratios for comparison

evidence.quote: From these observations $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C isotope ratios of 40$\pm$10, $\sim$50, and 40–50, respectively, were determined.

recipe.method: CASA 4.2 pipeline calibration and imaging; GILDAS analysis of line images
Reconstruct ALMA data with single-dish beams and compare integrated fluxes with published single-dish values
Ratio of velocity-integrated intensities where 13CN detected at S/N >~ 5 sigma
Opacity-corrected 12CN intensities divided by 1.082 x I(13CN)

evidence.quote: range from 30 to 67 with an average of 41.6 $\pm$ 0.2 in NGC 253
from 24 to 62 with an average of 38.3 $\pm$ 0.4 in NGC 1068
from 6 to 44 with an average of 16.9 $\pm$ 0.3 in NGC 4945
an average of 30.0 $\pm$ 0.2 (errors given here and elsewhere are standard deviations of the mean) in NGC 253
the derived optical depths of $^{12}$CN $J$ = 3/2–1/2 are 1.1, 0.7, and 0.8 in NGC 253, NGC 1068, and NGC 4945, respectively

not_stated_but_needed: Imaging parameters (weighting, robust, cell size, image size, deconvolver, masks)
Velocity integration ranges for each hyperfine group
How 13CN S/N >= 5 sigma masking and pixel sampling were done
Procedure for convolving ALMA data to single-dish beams for missing flux
Mapping of 13CN hyperfine group to J components in Eq. 2 per pixel

score_reason: Simple ratio method with stated equations, but imaging and integration details are unspecified.
